content: It is only with the heart that one can see rightly; what is essential is invisible to the eye.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
sourceWork: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

In Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: Who in your life needs your unconditional support or appreciation today without any transaction?
